To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BBL sugar-specific recognition is not limited to the glycoprotein of the major 14 kDa lectin but extends to other brain stem glycoprotein subunits.

the 84 kDA subunit of the soluble brain stem glycoprotein and an alkaline PAGE fast migrating glycoprotein of 55 kDA are sugar-specifically recognized in the bovine brain stem, by an endogenous 14kDA galactose-binding protein.
the 55 kDa-58 kDa glycoproteins and the 84 kDal subunit, which were sugar-specifically recognized in bovine brains, are the complementary glycoprotein receptors for BBL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, characterization and identification of the complementary glycoprotein(s) recognized by endogenous BBL in brain stem.
the identification of the complementary glycoprotein(s) that are recognized by BBL and the characterization of their carbohydrate composition.
the isolation and characterization of a 55 kDa/58 kDa glycoproteins from bovine brain stem which are the complementary glycoprotein(s) recognized by the endogenous lectins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sugar-specifically recognized receptors for BBL are the 55 kDa-58 kDa glycoproteins and the 84 k Da glycoprotein.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BBL recognizes chiefly the 84 k Da subunit and the 55 kDa-58 kDa fast moving glycoproteins.
BBL is a sugar-specific lectin which is present in soluble brain stem glycoprotein preparations and recognizes a 55 kDa glycoproteins subunit.
BBL recognizes in soluble brain stem glycoprotein extracts a 58-84 kDa glycosylated protein(s) which is distinct from membrane-bound glycoproteins and from the 55 kDa glycoproteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 14 kDa BBL sugar-specific recognition is not limited to membrane glycoproteins and is not restricted by the presence or absence of sialic acids on glycoproteins.
the endogenous lectins of brain stem are not only sugar-specific but also have specificity for the carbohydrate composition of glycoproteins.
the sugar specificity of BBL can be utilized to identify and isolate its complementary glycoprotein(s) which may serve as its receptor.
